narrative:
The loan decision you received was based on an analysis of your application compared to others, and while the model saw potential in your situation, it also identified some factors that made the risk of repayment too high for approval. The model estimated that there was a **39% chance** you might struggle to repay the loan as agreed. Since the bank uses a threshold of 25% as the cutoff for approval, this placed your application in the "denied" category.

The decision wasn’t made lightly—three key aspects of your application stood out as the most influential in pushing the prediction toward a higher risk. First, the **length of time you’ve been planning this loan** was much shorter than average. Most approved applicants had been preparing for **18 months or more**, while your request was only for **6 months**. A longer planning period often signals better financial readiness, so this shorter timeline raised some concerns.

Second, the **type of checking account you have** played a role. While many approved applicants had some savings or income tied to their accounts, yours shows **no activity at all**, which can indicate limited financial stability. This was a significant factor in the decision, as it suggested you might have fewer financial buffers if unexpected expenses arise.

Finally, the **reason you’re seeking the loan**—purchasing a **new car**—was less common among approved applicants, who more often used loans for essentials like furniture or repairs. While buying a car can be a smart investment, the model may have seen this as a higher-risk expense, especially given the other factors in your application.

To improve your chances next time, consider addressing these areas: **extending your planning period**, **building some savings or demonstrating regular income activity**, and **exploring whether the loan purpose could be framed differently**—perhaps combining it with other financial goals. Taking steps to strengthen these aspects could make a meaningful difference in future applications.

The target variable is whether the applicant will be a bad credit risk.

Protected attributes sex, age and foreign_worker were not used to make the machine prediction.

A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward bad credit risk, negative toward good credit risk. Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.
